2702. /// Spin-based Read-write Lock
2703. ///
2704. /// # Overview
2705. ///
2706. /// This lock allows for multiple readers, or at most one writer to access
2707. /// at any point in time. The writer of this lock has exclusive access to
2708. /// modify the underlying data, while the readers are allowed shared and
2709. /// read-only access.
2710. ///
2711. /// The writing and reading portions cannot be active simultaneously, when
2712. /// one portion is in progress, the other portion will spin-wait. This is
2713. /// suitable for scenarios where the lock is expected to be held for short
2714. /// periods of time, and the overhead of context switching is higher than
2715. /// the cost of spinning.
2716. ///
2717. /// In addition to traditional read and write locks, this implementation
2718. /// provides the upgradeable read lock (`upread lock`). The `upread lock`
2719. /// can be upgraded to write locks atomically, useful in scenarios
2720. /// where a decision to write is made after reading.
2721. ///
2722. /// The type parameter `T` represents the data that this lock is protecting.
2723. /// It is necessary for `T` to satisfy [`Send`] to be shared across tasks and
2724. /// [`Sync`] to permit concurrent access via readers. The [`Deref`] method (and
2725. /// [`DerefMut`] for the writer) is implemented for the RAII guards returned
2726. /// by the locking methods, which allows for the access to the protected data
2727. /// while the lock is held.
2728. ///
2729. /// # Usage
2730. /// The lock can be used in scenarios where data needs to be read frequently
2731. /// but written to occasionally.
2732. ///
2733. /// Use `upread lock` in scenarios where related checking is performed before
2734. /// modification to effectively avoid deadlocks and improve efficiency.
2735. ///
2736. /// This lock should not be used in scenarios where lock-holding times are
2737. /// long as it can lead to CPU resource wastage due to spinning.
2738. ///
2739. /// # About Guard
2740. ///
2741. /// See the comments of [`SpinLock`].
2742. ///
2743. /// # Examples
2744. ///
2745. /// ```
2746. /// use ostd::sync::RwLock;
2747. ///
2748. /// let lock = RwLock::new(5)
2749. ///
2750. /// // many read locks can be held at once
2751. /// {
2752. ///     let r1 = lock.read();
2753. ///     let r2 = lock.read();
2754. ///     assert_eq!(*r1, 5);
2755. ///     assert_eq!(*r2, 5);
2756. ///
2757. ///     // Upgradeable read lock can share access to data with read locks
2758. ///     let r3 = lock.upread();
2759. ///     assert_eq!(*r3, 5);
2760. ///     drop(r1);
2761. ///     drop(r2);
2762. ///     // read locks are dropped at this point
2763. ///
2764. ///     // An upread lock can only be upgraded successfully after all the
2765. ///     // read locks are released, otherwise it will spin-wait.
2766. ///     let mut w1 = r3.upgrade();
2767. ///     *w1 += 1;
2768. ///     assert_eq!(*w1, 6);
2769. /// }   // upread lock are dropped at this point
2770. ///
2771. /// {
2772. ///     // Only one write lock can be held at a time
2773. ///     let mut w2 = lock.write();
2774. ///     *w2 += 1;
2775. ///     assert_eq!(*w2, 7);
2776. /// }   // write lock is dropped at this point
2777. /// ```
2778. ///
2779. /// [`SpinLock`]: super::SpinLock
2780. pub struct RwLock<T  /* : ?Sized*/ , Guard /* = PreemptDisabled*/ > {
2781.     guard: PhantomData<Guard>,
2782.     /// The internal representation of the lock state is as follows:
2783.     /// - **Bit 63:** Writer lock.
2784.     /// - **Bit 62:** Upgradeable reader lock.
2785.     /// - **Bit 61:** Indicates if an upgradeable reader is being upgraded.
2786.     /// - **Bits 60-0:** Reader lock count.

2797.         let has_writer_bit: bool = (v & WRITER) != 0;

2804.         // NOTE: This does not mean there are actually this number of active `RwLockReadGuard`s. The actual number of successfully

2809.         // The number is tracked by the ghost resources remained in the lock.
2810.         // By active, we mean from the perspective the lock, the permissions for these guards are given out.

2823.         };

2830.             g.read_guard_token is Left
2831.         } else {

2836.         &&& has_upgrade_bit <==> (active_upgrade_guard || pending_failed_upread_attempt)

2838.         &&& !(active_upgrade_guard && pending_failed_upread_attempt)
2839.         // The `READER` bits count the number of all active read guards and pending failed `try_read` attempts.

2848.         &&& g.core_token.wf()
2849.         &&& g.core_token.is_left() ==> {
